issues.quote: Why: the same time pair repeats in 20 of 47 untaken-offer threads across 10 of 14 sampled rooftops, and the written rule against it is not holding [E2, E42, E15].
issues.concern: This is the base-versus-one-off sentence in the Decision, and it merges two numbers. E42 says the 47 untaken-offer threads span 10 rooftops. It does not say how many rooftops the 20 repeats span. Two stores carry 27 of the 47. For all I know the 20 repeats sit mostly at those two stores. If a CSM tells a dealer group 'this happens at 10 of 14 stores', we are quoting a figure we never measured.
issues.because: E42, E2; missing (rooftop spread of the 20 repeat threads and of the 12 silent threads)
issues.ask: Reword it as: '47 untaken-offer threads across 10 of 14 sampled rooftops; of these, 20 repeated the same pair'. Or add the rooftop count for the 20 repeats, with the two concentrated stores shown apart. Make the same fix to the Breadth line (line 45).

issues.quote: | Agent-set visits per 100 engaged SMS leads, per rooftop (primary) | 19 of 100 offered two times | up, counting only visits with a CRM id | [E5, E89] |
issues.concern: This is the one number phase 1 will be judged on, and it cannot be judged. First, the baseline and the after are different measures. 'Today' counts every booking among leads offered two times (E5). 'After' counts only bookings with a CRM id, and only 18 of 319 VinSolutions visits carry one (E89). Second, the name says 'engaged leads' but the baseline is 'offered two times'. Third, 'up' is not a target, and nothing says what result takes the pilot to every SMS rooftop (line 9) or what result stops it. Fourth, the only guard against pushy re-offers is show rate, and the page says show rate is 'not measurable'. In a quarter I will be asked whether this worked, and this row cannot answer.
issues.ask: Restate the baseline on the same definition as the after: same denominator, CRM-id visits only, per rooftop, over a pre-period. Set a minimum lift and a read date that decide pilot-to-base, and a kill line. Add one guard you can measure now, such as opt-out or STOP replies after a re-offer per rooftop (see request), next to show rate.

issues.quote: **Flywheel stage:** lead to appointment, on SMS, before the lead goes back to the BDC
issues.concern: Unfixed from ceo-r1-5. This is the handoff fact five is about, and the page still never names it as one. When Vini does not set the visit, the lead passes to the BDC or a salesperson, and a trade-in goes to the used-car desk. Phase 1 also leaves that handoff exactly as it is: an idle summary note, deferred to RETCONVAI-5165 (line 61). What phase 1 changes is when Vini stops talking. I still cannot tell who at the store benefits, who signs and who can kill it. The GM in E35 wants these leads on the phone, and the used car manager in E34 thinks the goal is too appointment-fixed. Either of them could pull the flag.
issues.because: E29, E33, E34, E35, E61; decide.md Inputs, Strategic fit (fact 5)
issues.ask: Add one line under Decision. Handoff: Vini to the BDC or internet sales on an unbooked lead, and to the used-car desk on a trade-in. Phase 1 changes when Vini stops, not what the person receives. Benefits: BDC manager (fewer re-touches, Q6). Signs: GM. May block: GSM or used car manager, on pushiness (E34, E35).

issues.quote: Action items keep blocking on DriveCentric and PBS, and everywhere on callback, lost lead, trade-in and Human Requested; elsewhere a photo or quote item stops cancelling the nudge. Q15 settles the list before ship [E61, E72, E73].
issues.concern: The skip rule now rests on 'a person holds the task', but the evidence does not show the right person holds it. On DriveCentric the task goes to the first user in the store's user list, or else the associated salesperson (E72). That may be an admin rather than whoever works the lead. On PBS the reminder names nobody unless a deal with a rep already exists (E73, line 31). PBS without a rep is the same situation the page uses to unblock other stores: no person holds the item. If that is wrong, the lead goes quiet with a task sitting in nobody's real queue, which is the E33 failure again.
issues.ask: On PBS, keep blocking only when the deal has a named SalesRep, and treat PBS without a rep like the note-only CRMs. On DriveCentric, confirm who 'first user in the store's user list' is at the 2 live DriveCentric rooftops before relying on it (see request), and add that to Q15.

issues.quote: [ASSUMPTION: phase 1 pilots first at rooftops whose CRM takes the visit as an appointment, not VinSolutions]
issues.concern: VinSolutions is the largest CRM in the SMS base by rooftop count: 11 rooftops and 319 SMS visits (E89). There the visit lands as one note line plus a stage change, under the Spyne integration user (E87). Line 9 says we build this for every SMS rooftop. This line quietly drops a third of the base from the pilot, and the page gives no plan for those stores. The table also leaves out the 8 rooftops whose CRM is unknown (321 visits, E89). For fact four I need the list, plus the plan for the rest.
issues.because: E87, E89; Q34; missing (whether a VinSolutions appointment write exists and its commercial status)
issues.ask: Add a 'CRM unknown, 8 rooftops' row to the table. Say what phase 1 does at VinSolutions rooftops: ships with the note-and-stage landing, waits, or waits on a negotiated appointment write with that provider, with an owner. Change line 9 to 'every SMS rooftop whose CRM takes the visit as an appointment' until then.
